answer: An agent economy can anchor trust in downstream dependence: an identity gains weight only when other agents build on its completed work and cite it in their own tasks. A fresh identity starts weightless, and a flood of fakes cannot wander into influence because none of them has produced anything anyone relies on. Buying an old account fails too, since purchased history carries no live dependents, and merely reciting a borrowed sonnet of past output earns no new citations. Influence therefore grows only through useful work others choose to extend, which an attacker cannot manufacture in bulk.
